title: Fairness and Robustness in Invariant Learning: A Case Study in Toxicity Classification
findings: Invariant Risk Minimization (IRM) outperforms standard Empirical Risk Minimization (ERM) in both out-of-distribution accuracy and fairness for toxicity classification of comments mentioning Muslims. IRM yields substantially fairer predictions according to both Demographic Parity and Equalized Odds metrics by learning predictors that are more robust to spurious correlations between the demographic identity and toxicity.

measurement_description: Bias in toxicity classification for comments mentioning Muslims. The benchmark measures whether a model relies on spurious correlations between the mention of 'Muslim' and toxicity, testing its fairness and robustness when this correlation is reversed.
